thesis: India's AI/data-centre buildout creates a multi-year capex chain: land & shells -> power generation/transmission -> transformers/switchgear/gensets -> cooling -> cables/fibre/networking -> servers/GPU compute. The demand side is not in doubt - Cummins reports data centres at 40% of powergen revenue, Blue Star booked Rs1,500 cr of DC MEP orders in one quarter, Hitachi Energy named 560+800 MVA of DC transformer orders, Schneider disclosed over a fifth of a record backlog in DC/semis/solar, and L&T won a Rs10,000-15,000 cr NVIDIA B300 AI Factory. Three things shape how to hold it. POWER is the binding constraint, not land: the government's own AI data-centre load estimate doubled to 26.3 GW by FY32, facilities build in 12-18 months against 3-5 years for grid, and the PM's 15 August address tied AI capacity to five new nuclear reactors this decade. The tax exemption is now LAW-IN-WAITING rather than a proposal - the Taxation and Other Laws Amendment Bill passed the Lok Sabha on 6 August and the Rajya Sabha on 10 August, widening eligibility to leased data centres and removing the dual-notification requirement (presidential assent unconfirmed). And the trigger for the August share-price move - a DRAFT US FCC ban on Chinese optical transceivers - has produced nothing in two weeks: no docket, no vote, no product definition, and Sterlite and HFCL have given back 3-4%. Much of this basket is levered to a US policy decision it does not control, with NVIDIA reporting 26 August and Broadcom 2 September.
method_note: Per SECTOR_INTELLIGENCE_FRAMEWORK.md: evidence is temporal and decays. Every evidence item is dated; order-win items have a half-life of roughly 1-3 weeks (interpretation) to quarters (earnings/guidance), while structural items (capacity plans, policy) last years. Exposure ratings are categorical states, not scores. Nothing here is a fair-value model - it is the L1 evidence layer for an AI-infra hypothesis set. The 12-month grade added on 2026-08-13 deliberately stores its THREE INPUTS separately (evidence quality, exposure purity, how much is priced in) rather than combining them into a number, because the framework's own rule is 'explicit categorical states + evidence, not invented scores'.

hypotheses.text: The August 2026 India AI-infra rally was triggered by a US TRADE action, not by India demand or policy
supporting: On 4 August 2026 Reuters reported the FCC is preparing an import ban on Chinese optical transceiver modules for US data centres; US optical names ripped (AAOI +20%, Coherent +18%, Lumentum +14%)
On 5 August STLTECH and HFCL each hit 5% upper circuits, explicitly attributed to those proposed curbs
No India policy event in the window is large enough to explain a sector-wide 10-33% move; the CBDT tax-relief FAQ (5 Aug) is real but technical and conditional on Parliament passing the bill
The Nifty went nowhere over the same period (24,570 on 7 Aug to 24,436 on 12 Aug) - this was a stock-specific move, not an index re-rating

TWO WEEKS ON, THE TRIGGER HAS PRODUCED NOTHING: no FCC docket, vote, comment period, product definition or implementation date; the 6 August FCC open meeting agenda contained no transceiver item, and no September agenda has been published. The likeliest vehicle is the existing 'Strengthening Rules Governing Dangerous Gear' framework adopted 22 July rather than a fresh rulemaking, which would explain the absence of a new docket - but that is inference. If the proposal is dropped, the August catalyst disappears entirely.
